newsitem.title: USA: IMF board to continue talks on Sudan on Monday.
newsitem.headline: IMF board to continue talks on Sudan on Monday.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund executive board met Friday on Sudan's financial situation and said it would continue on Monday in talks that could lead to a recommendation that the country be expelled.
The 24-member board is considering an almost unprecedented action against one of the IMF's 181 member countries because Sudan has refused to address its $1.7 billion in arrears to the Fund.
However, even if it were to take this action, it would require an 85 percent majority of member countries votes for to remove the African state, one of the poorest countries in the world.
Monetary sources have expressed the view that this would be difficult to achieve since developing countries would be relunctant to kick out one of their own.

While some countries have chosen to leave the lending institution voluntarily, IMF records show only one country -- Czechoslovakia -- was compelled to withdraw because it refused to provide required economic data in the early 1950s.
As it now stands, Sudan is one of four countries ineligible to borrow from the IMF because of overdue loans and has also lost its voting rights in the institution.
